name: South Slavey

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of South Slavey (sout2959).

notes:
Northern Athabaskan (Dene) language of the Dehcho region of the Northwest Territories, in its practical Roman orthography. The obstruents carry the Athabaskan three-way laryngeal contrast: ⟨b d g dz j dl ddh⟩ are the plain (voiceless unaspirated) series, ⟨t k ts ch tl/tł tth⟩ the aspirated series, and an apostrophe writes the ejective. Unaspirated obstruents range from voiceless to weakly voiced across speakers and dialects, so both realizations are listed with the voiceless one first, and the prenasalized pair ⟨mb⟩ ⟨nd⟩ carries the same two-way listing. ⟨l⟩ is the voiced lateral fricative [ɮ] against voiceless ⟨ł⟩ [ɬ]; ⟨y⟩ is [j] with a [ʒ] variant attested in the narrow transcriptions. Labialization is allophonic, not phonemic, so ⟨kw⟩ is /k/ + /w/ and gets no key of its own. Both apostrophe characters are accepted (U+02BC and ASCII), and both ⟨ɂ⟩ and a bare apostrophe write the glottal stop, since published South Slavey materials use each. ⟨r⟩ is not in the South Slavey letter inventory at all and turns up only in borrowings, so it keeps a plain rhotic reading: the flap the sources describe belongs to Hare, and the narrow transcriptions' [ɾ] is not adopted on a Hare statement.

Tone is written on every vowel: the acute marks high tone and the unmarked vowel is low, which the spec spells out with a grave, because low is a tone and not the absence of one. The ogonek writes nasalization and combines with the acute. A doubled vowel letter is one long nucleus. The lax /i/ alternant the source states is encoded, for the ORAL vowel only, in the non-final-nucleus environment the transcriptions actually draw for it (see the rule note, which says plainly which half of that is the source's and which is not). The source also states an [æ] alternant of ⟨e⟩ before a back vowel; it is NOT encoded, because [æ] does not occur once in the WikiPron South Slavey gold, so there is nothing to check an operationalization of that environment against. The gold does write [e] for ⟨e⟩ in five words (⟨jíye⟩, ⟨jíyetú⟩, ⟨dúyé⟩, ⟨ɂeghú⟩, ⟨ɂetthí⟩) in no environment either source describes — and [e] is the value of ⟨ə⟩, a vowel the source says South Slavey does not have — so that is left alone as well. One further convention is deliberately not followed: the gold lowers /o/ to [o̞], which no source states and which the benchmark's narrow-diacritic normalization strips anyway.

sources.notes: Source of the consonant chart (plain p t ts tɬ tʃ k against aspirated tʰ tsʰ tɬʰ tʃʰ kʰ and the ejectives), the statement that unaspirated obstruents are voiceless or weakly voiced, the prenasalized stops /ᵐb, ⁿd/, the velar fronting and labialization allophony, the /ɬ/ vs /ɮ/ lateral contrast, the two-tone system with acute for high and unmarked low, ogonek nasalization, and vowel length written /VV/. The vowel chart is the source for ⟨a⟩ = [a], ⟨o⟩ = [o], ⟨u⟩ = [u], and for BOTH alternants of the two vowels that have them: ⟨i⟩ = "[i] or [ɪ] in syllable onset" and ⟨e⟩ = "[ɛ] or [æ] when followed by a back vowel". The same page's flap statement is explicitly about Hare, not South Slavey, which is why ⟨r⟩ is not read as [ɾ] here.

sources.author: McDonough, Joyce (ed.)
sources.title: Dene Speech Atlas: Orthography for South Slavey
sources.notes: Letter inventory consulted for this spec: the obstruent letters b d t tʼ g k kʼ ddh tth tthʼ dz ts tsʼ dl tł tłʼ j ch chʼ dh th s z ł sh zh x gh h ʔ and the sonorant letters l m mb n nd w y, and the five-vowel system with length, nasalization and tone. The page carries no IPA, so nothing here takes a phonetic value from it; ⟨r⟩ is absent from its inventory entirely.

allophone_rules.notes: Velar obstruents front to a palatal before front vowels and labialize before round vowels (Wikipedia, 'Slavey language', phonology section, which gives /kɛ/ → [cɛ]); the narrow WikiPron South Slavey transcriptions show the ejective ⟨kʼ⟩ staying plain in both environments, so the rule is written for the plain and aspirated velars only.

Syllable-final ⟨h⟩ before a consonant is a coda /h/, realized as voiceless offglide (preaspiration) on the preceding vowel rather than as a separate [h]; coda /h/ and preaspiration are the same object (Wikipedia, 'Preaspiration'). Intervocalic and word-final ⟨h⟩ keep [h].

The source gives ⟨i⟩ as "[i] or [ɪ] in syllable onset". A vowel is not a syllable onset, so that environment cannot be applied as written; what it is operationalized as here is the word's last nucleus versus every earlier one, which is the split the WikiPron narrow transcriptions draw for ORAL /i/ without exception across all 146 words (⟨lidí⟩ [ɮɪ̀tí], ⟨ɂamíi⟩ [ʔàmɪ́ì]). Nasal /ĩ/ does NOT lax: ⟨tlįah⟩, ⟨tlįcho⟩, ⟨tlįsho⟩ and ⟨tsʼélįah⟩ all keep [ĩ] in a non-final nucleus, so this rule is keyed to the oral vowel and leaves the ogonek vowels alone. The alternant itself is the source's; its conditioning environment is not, and a South Slavey reference grammar should be consulted to replace it.
